# Annual Infrastructure Review

This report summarizes infrastructure spend and reliability across the fiscal year, drawing on the finance export dated 2026-08-01 and the incident log maintained by the platform team. Compute spend rose steadily through the first three quarters before leveling off in the fourth as the migration to reserved instances completed. Storage costs grew faster than compute in relative terms, largely due to the retention policy change adopted in March, which extended log retention from thirty to ninety days across every service. Reliability, measured as the fraction of five-minute windows with zero paging alerts, improved from 97.2% to 99.1% over the same period, with the largest single gain following the rollout of the new deployment pipeline in June. Two significant incidents occurred: one in April caused by a misconfigured autoscaling policy, and one in September caused by a downstream provider outage outside the team's control. Both are described in detail in the appendix, along with the remediation steps taken and their current status. Source: finance export 2026-08-01; platform incident log; deployment pipeline changelog. Looking ahead, the team recommends continuing the reserved-instance strategy, revisiting the retention policy given its cost impact, and adding an automated canary check ahead of the next major dependency upgrade to reduce the risk of a repeat of the April incident.
